scores.evidence: The screen-flow diagram (s2-b3/s2-b4 area, 'アプリを開く → 今月の残り画面 ⇄ 支出の入力画面') is readable at 390 px. Its labels are in the correct language in JP and EN, and it has a caption and a '図の説明を読む' toggle. Both tables (s2-table, the MoSCoW table) wrap cleanly on mobile, and no metric reports overflow, broken images or mermaid errors.

No screen is text-only. Each section breaks up its prose with definitions, a table, a callout or a check. Two minor points: desktop JP charsPerLine max is 42 (target 30–40, median 37 is fine), and the 6-question exam runs about 5 mobile screens with no break (mobile-jp-16..21).

The EN screenshots have no leftover Japanese: headings, tables, diagram nodes, the prompt and quiz options are all translated. JP has no awkward breaks inside words, contrast is good, and no controls are hidden under the 56/60 px bars on mobile. EN charsPerLine median 73 is within 60–75 (max 78).

niceToHave: reader: on mobile the flashcard hint reads 'クリックまたはスペースキーでめくる' (pages/mobile-jp-23.png). On touch devices show a tap hint instead.

reader: the knowledge-check block shows all 6 questions as one long card on mobile (pages/mobile-jp-16.png to mobile-jp-21.png). A per-question pager or a sticky '6問中 n問目' would make it easier to find your place.
s2-defs: in the desktop JP definition rows the last line holds only 'す。' or 'れる」の形で…' (pages/desktop-jp-04.png). Trimming a few characters, e.g. '入力欄や画面、通知など、アプリが「すること」。', would avoid the orphan.
s3-steps: the 6-step worked example takes about 3.5 mobile screens of continuous text (pages/mobile-jp-11.png to mobile-jp-14.png). Shortening each step's body to one sentence would tighten it.
summary: The lesson looks clean in all three renders: no overflow, console errors or broken visuals, and a full EN translation. Every section is broken up by a definition list, table, diagram or check. Nothing has to be fixed. The only content polish is minor: orphaned line endings in the s2-defs rows and a slightly long s3-steps worked example on mobile.
